transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m mostly here because my sleep has become really unreliable. Even when I’m exhausted, I’ll lie awake replaying work forecasts and team issues. Then I wake up around three or four in the morning and can’t get my brain to shut down again.
Outside of your sleep difficulties, have you been feeling persistently down or depressed?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed feeling persistently down, exactly.
During the day, do you find yourself worrying excessively about different everyday matters?

Yes, most days. My mind just jumps from one thing to another—whether we’ll hit the launch numbers, whether someone on my team might quit, then the mortgage or a client renewal. Even a small delay can start to feel like it’s going to turn into something much bigger.
How long have you been dealing with this persistent, everyday worry?
It’s been building since the sales division reorganization, so about thirteen months now.
Do you find it difficult to control or stop these worries once they start?
Yes. I’ll tell myself, “Brenda, you’ve made the plan, let it go,” but five minutes later I’m in another loop. I can resolve one concern, and then three more pop up.
Have you noticed physical signs of tension, such as tightness in your neck or shoulders, or aching muscles?
Yes. I feel wound up almost all the time, even at home just eating dinner. My shoulders stay tight no matter how much I try to relax.
